headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from Perplexity’s browser-based RAG into RisingWave’s data-engineering context; no direct shared-channel evidence for higher severity.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Perplexity can run browser-based Pro Search and ingest uploaded documents, so it may surface untrusted web text. RisingWave is a data-engineering system with no documented parser hardening or provenance checks in this profile. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly evidenced, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Perplexity output is copied into RisingWave SQL, configs, or ETL prompts without review
IF RisingWave consumes Perplexity-generated text as instructions or code
mitigations: Require manual review of all Perplexity-derived text before use
Strip instructions from retrieved web content before passing it onward
Use a fixed template for any Perplexity-to-RisingWave handoff
Disable any automation that treats search output as executable input
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between retrieval and downstream use

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and can handle uploaded documents and browsing context, while RisingWave has no network egress and no documented data classes touched. There is no shared workspace or direct transfer path in the profiles, so leakage is not evidenced; the remaining risk is limited to manual movement of content.
conditions: IF uploaded documents from Perplexity contain sensitive data and are manually pasted into RisingWave workflows
IF an operator exports Perplexity browsing context into RisingWave inputs
mitigations: Avoid moving sensitive documents between the tools
Redact identifiers before any manual transfer
Use separate accounts and workspaces
Review Perplexity privacy settings before uploading files
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on any export/import path

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Perplexity has no filesystem write, shell, or git modification capability, and RisingWave is only described as a data-engineering system with network egress none. No overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource is documented, so a capability conflict pathway is not plausible from the profiles.
conditions: IF a separate orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not grant shared write credentials
Verify no external orchestrator adds a common mutable target

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity produces cited answers from live search, and RisingWave is a data-engineering system that could plausibly consume those outputs as inputs. Because no verification or approval step is documented between them, erroneous Perplexity output could cascade into downstream transformations or operational decisions. The interaction is inferred, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF RisingWave ingests Perplexity-generated text, SQL, or schema suggestions without validation
IF Perplexity output is treated as authoritative in an ETL or materialized-view workflow
mitigations: Require a human verification step before ingestion
Compare Perplexity outputs against source-of-truth data
Log and review any downstream actions triggered by retrieved text
Use schema validation before applying suggestions
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity’s profile shows uploaded documents and browsing context, but no specific residency or retention mismatch is documented for RisingWave. Because the pair lacks explicit compliance metadata on the B side, only a limited compliance-gap risk is supportable, and the other agent is not cited beyond its absence of relevant controls.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into Perplexity and later exported into a separate compliance regime
IF retention or residency requirements are imposed externally on the workflow
mitigations: Avoid regulated data uploads
Check vendor privacy terms before use
Keep a record of what data was uploaded
Use a separate compliant system for regulated workloads
requires-engineering: map data flows to residency and retention controls
